subject: [AMBER] Water bridge formed between protein and ligand

messages.author: Shakuntala Dhurua
messages.body:
Hi everyone,
I want to check a water bridge formed between protein and ligand in my system such as protein-water-ligand. I tried this command ==> hbond All out All.hbvtime.dat solventdonor :WAT solventacceptor :WAT.O* avgout All.UU.avg.dat solvout All.UV.avg.dat bridgeout All.bridge.avg.dat but I am not clear about out file All.bridge.avg.dat file, how it formed bridge between them exactly. The All.bridge.avg.dat file was generated by such data such as below
Bridge Res 33:GLU  34:LEU , 789 frames.
Bridge Res 15:ARG  57:GLU , 742 frames.
Bridge Res 48:ILE  60:LEU , 705 frames.
which I am not looking for, Is there any other way of analyzing protein-water-ligand bridges? and also what does it mean which was generated in out file All.bridge.avg.dat. Please help me to understand.
Any help will be highly appreciated. Thank you in advance.

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
On Mon, Apr 4, 2022 at 9:39 AM Shakuntala Dhurua <518cy6026.nitrkl.ac.in> wrote:
> which I am not looking for,
We could probably help better if you describe what you are looking for
specifically.
> Is there any other way of analyzing protein-water-ligand bridges? and also what does it mean which was generated in out file All.bridge.avg.dat. Please help me to understand.
Please read the 'hbond' command entry in the Amber or Cpptraj manuals
(e.g.
https://jenkins.jasonswails.com/job/amber-github/job/cpptraj/job/master/lastSuccessfulBuild/artifact/doc/CpptrajManual.pdf
).
You might try the 'bridgebyatom' keyword which will report bridging
results by atom instead of by residue. If you use the GitHub version
of cpptraj (
https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj
) you can use the
recently added bridging time series keywords (see
https://github.com/Amber-MD/cpptraj/pull/948
) to get a time series for
each detected bridge.
Hope this helps,
-Dan
>
> Any help will be highly appreciated. Thank you in advance.
>
>

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
On Mon, Apr 4, 2022 at 1:24 PM Shakuntala Dhurua <518cy6026.nitrkl.ac.in> wrote:
>
> Thank you for your suggestion. But can we check any water molecule forming bridge between protein and ligand by using cpptraj ? like protein-water-ligand. example LYS-water-SO3, here LYS is protein part whereas SO3 is ligand part, so can we analyse water as a bridge between protein and ligand by using cpptraj?
Yes, the SO3 should be picked up if you aren't specifying any
particular mask. Otherwise you can explicitly select it like:
hbond :SO3,<mask selecting protein>
You may also want to add the 'nointramol' keyword if you're not
interested in intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Hope this helps,
-Dan
